source.title: Towards Accelerating Training of Batch Normalization: A Manifold Perspective
source.authors: Ming-Yang Yi; Qi Meng; Wei Chen; Zhi-Ming Ma

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation affecting the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-error convergence comparisons for BN ResNets on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but does not measure whether the stated methods reach zero or near-zero training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper says it reports training error in Figure 3 and states that PSI-SGD and PSI-SGDM converge faster than three baselines after 120 epochs. It gives no textual endpoint values for training error; test accuracies in Table 1 are not training-error results. Figure-only curves are recorded without estimating values.
record.test_reason: Section 6.2 reports training-error curves for SGD and Adam on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 ResNets, matching V1's method and measure. However, the supplied text omits the plotted values and never states whether training error reaches zero or near zero, so it cannot establish a verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: PSI optimization removes ambiguity between positively scale-equivalent weights, has convergence guarantees, and reportedly improves convergence and generalization. Their comparative claims are not uniform numerical wins: some test accuracies tie or fall below SGDG, and per-epoch runtimes exceed SGD's.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares proposed manifold-based optimization methods with SGD, Adam, and SGDG on BN networks; it does not test the full recipe in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, ResNet depth, and optimization algorithm are varied in the experiments; the paper states the proposed methods converge faster than the baselines after 120 epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: PSI-SGD and PSI-SGDM reportedly reduce training error faster than optimizer baselines after 120 epochs in BN ResNets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing scale-invariant parameters on the PSI manifold can accelerate training relative to Euclidean optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 4 reports poor SGD training under unbalanced weight scaling in a two-layer BN network on MNIST, while PSI-SGD performs better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Functionally equivalent initial weight scales can affect SGD optimization in batch-normalized networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems and the toy experiment concern convergence of gradient norms rather than zero classification error or the other specified effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PSI optimization improves convergence bounds and empirical gradient-norm convergence under the studied assumptions and settings.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence (UAI 2022)
record.problems: Training-error outcomes are presented in figures, without endpoint values or textual claims about reaching zero or near-zero error. The paper does not state initialization details in the supplied experimental setup.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: Figure 3 is described as reporting training error and faster convergence, but the text does not assign a training-error endpoint to any individual model, dataset, or algorithm. Table 1 reports test accuracy, not the claim's training-error measure.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels; smaller-model and early-stopping comparisons; initialization is unspecified. The clean-label training-error endpoints cannot be determined from the supplied figure captions and prose.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training degradation in plain networks versus identity-shortcut networks; special tanh initialization and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization in plain networks.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature evolution, and divergence.
Matched comparisons with and without batch normalization, higher learning-rate tolerance attributable to BN, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The omitted training-error curves are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not additional missing results. Table 1 and Table 2 report test accuracy and cannot establish V1. Faster convergence alone establishes neither near-zero training error nor its absence. Weight-scale sensitivity in BN networks does not test V4's specified initialization mechanisms, and comparisons among optimizers with BN do not test V6.

versions.untested_parts: Whether SGD or Adam reach zero or near-zero training classification error; corrupted or random labels; smaller models and early stopping.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
